notes:
BATCH AH (topical: betamethasone-miconazole-gentamicin, triamcinolone-nystatin-neomycin, clotrimazole, mupirocin, silver-sulfadiazine, povidone-iodine, calamine-zinc-oxide). All quotes checked FOUND with the same normalisation as fetchtext --check / verify.mjs. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked).
NO UK PRODUCT (availability no-uk-product, rules []): (1) betamethasone-miconazole-gentamicin: no UK three-ingredient product, and no UK gentamicin product for the skin at all (UK gentamicin = injections and eye/ear drops). The clinic monograph's two emc links are single-ingredient miconazole 2% cream and betamethasone dipropionate cream; they were not used to build the combination (same approach as batch L amlodipine-valsartan-hydrochlorothiazide). (2) triamcinolone-nystatin-neomycin: no UK topical triamcinolone product of any kind; the clinic monograph's emc link (12947) is clobetasol/neomycin/nystatin ointment (very potent steroid, age and dose limits specific to clobetasol), so not used. Consequence: the expected neomycin/gentamicin ototoxicity statements are NOT in the KB for these two medicines (they exist only in UK products that are not the clinic product).
SUBSTITUTE / NON-EMC SOURCES: silver sulfadiazine and povidone-iodine have no emc SmPC; UK SPCs were read from MHRA products PDFs (mhraproducts4853 blob URLs, found via the products.mhra.gov.uk search index). Silver sulfadiazine = the clinic product's own UK licence (1% cream, PL 13374/0006, text revised 02/07/2023). Povidone-iodine: no UK ointment exists; the clinic 10% ointment uses the UK 5% w/w cream SPC (PL 58442/0003; same ingredient and skin route, different strength/base, stated in the formulation note); the clinic dry powder spray uses the UK 2.5% cutaneous spray powder SPC (PL 58442/0001). The UK 10% alcoholic tincture SPC (PL 04509/0030, pre-operative skin disinfection) was read but NOT used: it is a different form; it contraindicates neonates, pregnancy and lactation and says avoid regular/prolonged use with thyroid disorders or lithium.
GROUPS: none added. Per instruction, topical products were NOT added to systemic groups (no sulfonamide, antibacterial, azole-antifungal or aminoglycoside membership). clotrimazole.json lists group imidazole-antifungal, whose clotrimazole membership is already sourced in batch AG (emc-2205). Allergy rules use allergen group:sulfonamide (silver sulfadiazine; members from batch F) and group:imidazole-antifungal (clotrimazole vaginal forms; members from batch AG).
SHARED SOURCES copied verbatim (same id and URL) from batch AG: emc-2205, sps-impetigo-topical-breastfeeding.
CONDITIONS: new latex-contraceptive-use, thyroid-dysfunction, radioiodine-procedure. Reused: undiagnosed-vaginal-bleeding (AE), moderate-severe-renal-impairment (Z), renal-impairment (A/C/G/Z), g6pd-deficiency, hypothyroidism, thyrotoxicosis (vocab). Povidone-iodine 'Thyroid dysfunction' is encoded on three conditions (thyroid-dysfunction, hypothyroidism, thyrotoxicosis) so it fires whichever the user picks.
LEVEL CHOICES: silver sulfadiazine 'at, or near term' is encoded as trimester 3 (contraindicated; concern says at/near term). Under-3-months age limit = 0.25 years (4.2 'contraindicated in children aged to three months'; 4.3 'premature infants or newborn infants during the first months of life'). Hepatic caution 'significant hepatic impairment' encoded as hepatic any (severity not defined). Oral hypoglycaemic interaction (large-area burns) mapped to group:oral-antidiabetic, level monitor, effect hypoglycaemia; phenytoin is not in the master list. Povidone-iodine + silver: 4.5 says mutual reduction of effects and 6.2 says should not be used together with silver salts, so level avoid with other = silver-sulfadiazine (rule on the povidone-iodine side only). Lithium (spray SPC: avoid prolonged use on extensive surfaces) and mercury products are text only (not in master list). Clotrimazole: latex contraceptive damage = caution condition rule (cream and vaginal forms; the solution SmPC does not state it); vaginal forms 'Not for use in children under 16' = avoid; 'over 60' and imidazole hypersensitivity = caution (medical advice must be sought); 'should not be used' with abnormal vaginal bleeding = avoid. Tacrolimus/sirolimus (vaginal clotrimazole) are text only. Mupirocin skin ointment 'should not be used' where large amounts of polyethylene glycol can be absorbed, especially moderate/severe renal impairment = avoid condition rule, ointment only (no numeric threshold).
CONFLICTS / DIFFERENCES BETWEEN UK SOURCES: (1) Clotrimazole pregnancy: SmPCs 'only under the supervision of a physician or midwife' vs BUMPS 'can be used ... first-choice treatment for thrush' (both kept; rule level caution). (2) Povidone-iodine breastfeeding: SPC 4.6 'should not be used during breastfeeding' vs SPC 4.4 'unless advised by your doctor ... only if clearly necessary' (same SPCs; rule level avoid, 4.4 wording kept as a detail item). (3) Mupirocin breastfeeding: SmPC gives no milk data; SPS says can be used, monitor infant for rash (rule level monitor). (4) Clotrimazole 500 mg: vaginal tablet SmPC says not for use under 16; 500 mg pessary SmPC says paediatric use not recommended.
NOT FOUND: no MHRA Drug Safety Update for clotrimazole, mupirocin, silver sulfadiazine or povidone-iodine (DSU keyword search); no BUMPS leaflet for mupirocin, povidone-iodine, silver sulfadiazine or calamine (404); no SPS breastfeeding page for clotrimazole, povidone-iodine or silver sulfadiazine (SPS clotrimazole pages found are PGD templates only, not used); SPS 'Choosing medicines in sulfonamide hypersensitivity' lists sulfadiazine as a sulfonamide antibiotic but does not mention silver sulfadiazine, so it was not cited. Calamine SmPC dated 2016 (latest on emc).
BRAND PRESCRIBING: none stated by any UK source accessed.
AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent second check, log in audit/AH-AI.md): all 5 clotrimazole, 2 mupirocin, silver sulfadiazine, 2 povidone-iodine and calamine sources re-read in sections 4.1-4.9 (+6.2 for povidone-iodine); licences confirmed current in the MHRA products index. Both triple combinations confirmed no-uk-product (MHRA index: triamcinolone only as an injection; gentamicin only injections and eye/ear drops; emc triamcinolone search: two discontinued injections and a nasal spray). Added: clotrimazole cream 4.3 nail/scalp rule (new condition nail-scalp-fungal-infection), clotrimazole breastfeeding rule, calamine pregnancy and breastfeeding info rules. Povidone-iodine 10% ointment kept on the 5% cream SPC (same active, different strength) with a note that the cream amounts do not transfer to the ointment. Small wording fixes listed in the audit log.
